title: Clinical course and outcomes of patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis before and after liver transplantation at University Hospital Essen
summary:
Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare chronic
inflammation of the bile ducts that often requires liver transplantation. This study analyzes anonymized medical records of all adult PSC patients at University Hospital Essen. It examines how the disease progresses before and after transplantation and
which factors influence the course. No patients will be contacted and no additional examinations will be performed.

interventions.name: Adult patients with confirmed primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) treated at University Hospital Essen. No intervention, retrospective analysis of anonymized routine clinical data.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Confirmed PSC according to EASL Clinical Practice Guidelines 2022; age ≥ 18 years at first presentation; at least one PSC-related contact at University Hospital Essen until the cut-oﬀ date 30 Nov 2026; suﬃcient documentation. PSC-AIH
overlap is included and analyzed separately.
Exclusion criteria:
Secondary sclerosing cholangitis of other cause (ischemic, IgG4-related, postoperative, parasitic); documented objection to scientific use of data; insuﬃcient documentation.
